profiles.name: Percy Hoskins
profiles.excerpt: Percy Hoskins brought real Scotland Yard case material into radio as a leading British crime reporter and research source for Whitehall 1212 and other true-crime broadcasts.
profiles.bio_html:
Percy Kellick Hoskins was a British crime journalist best known for his long career with the Daily Express, where he became chief crime reporter. His professional authority came from reporting rather than acting, and his access to police cases made him valuable to broadcasters seeking authentic crime material.

Radio drew directly on that expertise. Hoskins supplied research and case material for Whitehall 1212, the NBC series based on files and objects from Scotland Yard's Black Museum, and he also contributed to Secrets of Scotland Yard. The surviving credits sometimes place him in performer fields because he could appear or be credited on broadcasts, but his central radio profession was research, story development and journalistic source work.

Golden Radio Hour preserves the complete 44-episode run of Whitehall 1212, whose cases repeatedly relied on Hoskins's crime-reporting research. His profile is therefore classified with writers and creators rather than actors, while the original archive credit data remains preserved.
